A notebook beside the estuary

The morning tide left small stories on the shore.

I took the long path with a pencil and a folded sheet of paper. Every bend offered something worth drawing, from wind-shaped grasses to the soft edges of a footprint.

Observations along the path

Tracks in the wet sand

Thin trails crossed the wet sand before disappearing into a shallow pool. I drew their intersections without trying to name every creature.

Field journal, early morning

Look closely

Return to the sand notes

Reeds bending into the wind

The reeds moved together until a gust separated their rhythms. Listening made the familiar path feel different.

Field journal, midday

Pause and listen

Return to the reed notes

Shadows across the boardwalk

Long shadows divided the boards into bands of light. The last drawing kept only those alternating shapes.

Field journal, late afternoon

Watch the light

Return to the shadow notes

The notebook came home full of unfinished lines. Leaving them unfinished felt like an invitation to return.
